Cause: ingest-worker is being OOMKilled (exit code 137) under morning batch load. Both pods show last_state "Terminated (OOMKilled), exit code 137" with a memory limit of only 512Mi. The pods carry the annotation `kubernetes.io/limit-ranger: "LimitRanger plugin set: memory request for container ingest-worker; memory limit for container ingest-worker"`, which means neither the request nor the limit are set in your manifest — they were injected by a LimitRange in the data-platform namespace. The old namespace evidently had no such LimitRange (or a higher default), so the same manifest ran unconstrained there. When a container has no memory limit of its own and runs in a namespace with a default memory limit, the control plane automatically assigns that default [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-memory-resource#if-you-do-not-specify-a-memory-limit-0][cite: tasks/administer-cluster/manage-resources/memory-default-namespace#create-a-limitrange-and-a-pod-0]. Memory limits are enforced by the kernel via OOM kills when the container exceeds them [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#requests-and-limits-1], producing exactly the OOMKilled / exit code 137 / restart pattern seen here [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-container-is-terminated-1].

Fix (owner can apply): explicitly set resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory in the ingest-worker Deployment to values that fit the batch workload (the old namespace behavior suggests well above 512Mi — start by sizing to observed peak RSS plus headroom). Explicit values in the pod spec override the LimitRange defaults [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/manage-resources/memory-default-namespace#what-if-you-specify-a-container-s-request-but-not-its-limit-1]. If the namespace LimitRange also enforces a `max` memory that is below what ingest-worker needs, you'll get a 403 at admission [cite: concepts/policy/limit-range#constraints-on-resource-limits-and-requests-0] and will need the data-platform admins to raise that max. Also consider whether the workload has a genuine memory leak before simply raising the limit [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-container-is-terminated-3].
